title: bd prime: custom PRIME.md drops memories; --memories-only ignores flag (GH#3941)
description:
WHAT: When a custom .beads/PRIME.md exists, `bd prime` outputs ONLY the custom content and silently drops the persistent memories section that the default template appends. And `bd prime --memories-only` outputs the full custom PRIME.md instead of just the memories. This breaks memory injection in hook contexts (PreCompact uses --memories-only).
WHERE: cmd/bd/prime.go primeCmd.Run (~lines 145-188): the custom-PRIME branch (lines 155-170) does `emit(content); return` BEFORE any memory logic and never consults primeMemoriesOnly (which is only handled later at line 178 via outputPrimeContextWithOptions -> outputMemoriesOnlyContext at 322-329). Memory rendering helper: formatMemoriesForPrime(compact bool) at 334-394.
HOW: Restructure Run BEFORE the custom-PRIME branch: (1) if primeMemoriesOnly, run outputMemoriesOnlyContext and return regardless of PRIME.md; (2) if a custom PRIME.md is found, emit its content PLUS formatMemoriesForPrime(false) when non-empty (matching default-template behavior), then return; (3) else existing default path. Optionally extract readCustomPrimeContent() to dedupe the three read sites. Update the cobra Long help wording that says custom PRIME replaces output 'entirely' (~line 99).
WHY: --memories-only is the primary memory-injection path for hooks; with a custom PRIME.md it returns zero memories, silently defeating bd remember.
Non-goals: NOT adding --no-memories here (that is GH#3961, sequenced after this); NOT adding --memories-cap; NOT changing memory storage.
PR: branch fix/3941-prime-memories-custom-primemd from origin/main -> gastownhall/beads. NOTE: prime_gemini_hook_test.go currently asserts verbatim custom-PRIME content and must be updated to expect appended memories.
close_reason: PR gastownhall/beads#4335 on branch fix/3941-prime-memories-custom-primemd (commit c55f7ac8c). Fix in cmd/bd/prime.go: --memories-only now handled before the custom-PRIME branch (returns only memories regardless of PRIME.md/--export); custom PRIME.md now appends formatMemoriesForPrime(false) when non-empty; readCustomPrimeContent() dedupes the 3 read sites; Long help wording updated. Evidence: TestPrime_CustomPrimeMd_AppendsMemories (custom content + Persistent Memories both present) and TestPrime_MemoriesOnly_WithCustomPrimeMd (memories present, custom content absent) PASS; existing Local/Global/Redirected/Default override tests still PASS. go test -tags gms_pure_go -run 'Prime|Codex' ./cmd/bd/ green.

title: claim() honors configured custom statuses (GH#4164)
description:
WHAT: `bd update <id> --claim` refuses to claim an issue whose status is a configured custom status (e.g. 'ready'), because claim SQL hard-codes the claimable predecessor as status='open'. Real downstream tools configure custom lifecycles (draft->...->ready->in_progress) where 'ready' should be claimable. Combined `--status in_progress --claim` also fails because claim runs before the status update.
WHERE: internal/storage/issueops/claim.go lines 53 and 59 (UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status='open' ...), both the StartedAt-nil and StartedAt-set branches. Also ClaimReadyIssueInTx line ~121 forces StatusOpen. Command layer: cmd/bd/update.go (claim runs at ~line 324 BEFORE the status UpdateIssue). Custom-status config + categories: internal/types/types.go (StatusCategory, ParseCustomStatusConfig, BuiltInStatusCategory) and internal/storage/issueops/config_helpers.go (ResolveCustomStatusesDetailedInTx).
HOW: Add a helper (e.g. ClaimableSourceStatusesInTx) returning {open} plus custom statuses whose category is 'active'. Change the claim UPDATE predicate from `status='open'` to `status IN (?,?...)`. Keep the assignee CAS guard and the idempotent same-actor in_progress branch unchanged. Do NOT add in_progress/blocked/hooked or wip/done/frozen customs to the claimable set (preserves the GH-3570 anti-steal protection). Align ClaimReadyIssueInTx similarly.
WHY: Custom statuses are a supported feature; claim being open-only silently breaks opinionated lifecycles. The status='open' guard was added in GH-3570 for atomic ready-claim safety — the fix must keep that.
Non-goals: NOT fixing the separate `--status open --claim` overwrite (BUG-29); NOT adding wip-category claimability; NOT changing bd ready's default status filter.
PR: branch fix/4164-claim-custom-statuses from origin/main -> gastownhall/beads.
close_reason: PR gastownhall/beads#4334 on branch fix/4164-claim-custom-statuses (commit e4c5a68d2). AC1: bd update <id> --claim succeeds from a custom active-category status (test TestClaimIssue_CustomStatuses, cc-ready -> in_progress assigned). AC2: claim rejected with ErrNotClaimable from custom wip status, issue left untouched (same test). AC3: built-in open still claimable + cross-actor anti-steal (ErrAlreadyClaimed) and idempotent same-actor re-claim preserved (TestClaimIssue_CustomActiveAntiSteal). Fix: ClaimIssueInTx uses status IN (open + active customs) via new ClaimableSourceStatusesInTx helper. Tests green: go test -tags gms_pure_go -run Claim ./internal/storage/....

title: Adopt centralized Linear sync architecture (Option 7)
description:
Implement the per-laptop reads + central CI writer architecture documented in [PLAN.md](<http://PLAN.md>) §5. Replaces the current per-laptop bidirectional sync model with one CI-mediated single writer to Linear and per-laptop read-only pulls. Eliminates conflict thrash, duplicate creation, and rate-limit storms on the write path.

Key design decisions resolved:

* External_ref storage separation: CI writes .beads/external_refs.json, devs write .beads/issues.jsonl ([PLAN.md](<http://PLAN.md>) §5)
* Bidirectional pull: PM-created Linear issues appear in devs' beads (decision d11)
* Disappearance policy: archive Linear issue when bead leaves JSONL (decision d12)
* Conflict policy: --prefer-linear on pulls (decision d5)
* Pull cadence: 15-min jittered cron (decision d8)

Depends on four architecture-blocker upstream PRs (PR-1, PR-3, PR-4, PR-5) under epic-upstream, plus the P0 security fix (PR-1) and privacy fix (wisp/memory leak bugs).

## Success criteria

* All 50 devs run bd linear sync --pull only locally (never push)
* One CI workflow is the sole bd linear sync --push invoker
* One OAuth client credential held in CI secrets, no personal API keys in any git-tracked file
* Every push to Linear is logged with bead_id, linear_id, outcome
* Sync success rate >= 99.5% over 50 consecutive runs in pilot
* Bead disappearance triggers Linear issue archival
* PM-created Linear issues flow to dev laptops on pull
close_reason: Architecture complete: all 4 critical-path PRs merged, CI worker built, pull cron ready, config/docs/monitoring/pilot plan shipped. Ready for pilot.

description:

Pre-create dedup query: use issues(filter: {description: {contains: "<marker>"}}) against the target team (validated 2026-05-02 in sandbox — see [PLAN.md](<http://PLAN.md>) §9 d13). If found, link existing as external_ref instead of creating duplicate.

## Acceptance criteria

* Hash formula uses only immutable fields (beads_id + creator_email + creation_ts_ns) — NOT title
* Dedup query uses issues(filter: {description: {contains: "<marker>"}}) — NOT searchIssues (exact match, no indexing delay)
* Sync interrupted between create and external_ref update; re-run sync detects existing Linear issue via marker, links it, no duplicate created
* Two devs creating beads with the same content: second push finds and links the first
* Roundtrip test with mock GraphQL
* Backward-compatible: existing Linear issues without markers still match via existing logic

## Non-goals

* Not changing the marker format (HTML comment is the interoperable choice)

description:

NOTE: the original issue #3965 is titled around `bd update`, which DOES touch last-touched on current main (update.go:531) — so this PR fixes the still-broken `bd close` case of the same contract and will say so transparently.
WHERE: cmd/bd/close.go — SetLastTouchedID is only called at line 239 for nextIssue.ID (--claim-next path), never for the closed issue(s). title: Upstream: ambient staleness signal — bd prime auto-pull + --pull-if-stale
description:
Add ambient staleness detection to bd so agents and devs automatically
get fresh Linear data without retry infrastructure.

## Background

Three adversarial reviewers (architecture, performance, agent-native)
converged: retry mechanisms (launchd, cron retries, daemons) are the
wrong layer. A missed cron pull isn't a failure to recover from — it's
a delay in an additive sync layer. The right answer is making staleness
visible so the tool auto-corrects.

Precedent: git's "your branch is behind", npm auto-install, cargo lock
auto-update — tools that fix their own preconditions beat advisory signals.

## Implementation

### 1\. `.beads/last_pull` timestamp file

* Written by `bd linear sync --pull` on success
* Contains ISO 8601 timestamp of last successful pull
* Cheap to stat/read — no database query needed
* Foundation for all staleness checks

### 2\. `bd linear sync --pull-if-stale [--threshold 20m]`

* Composable primitive: pulls only if last_pull > threshold (default 20m)
* 5-minute local debounce: if a pull happened in the last 5 min, no-op
* Returns `is_fresh` flag in JSON output for agent consumption
* Per-session and per-hour caps (5/session, 8/hour) to prevent loops

### 3\. `bd prime` auto-pull

* During orientation, check `.beads/last_pull`
* If stale (>20 min), run pull automatically before emitting orientation
* Agents already run `bd prime` at session start — zero config needed

### 4\. Staleness warning for humans (stderr, first invocation only)

* On any `bd` command, if last pull >20 min ago, emit once per session:
  "⚠ Linear data is 45m stale — run `bd linear sync --pull` to refresh"
* Suppress after first warning in the session (use temp file or env flag)
* Do NOT add this to agent rules — let bd own it

### 5\. Keep 15-min cron unchanged

* Background heartbeat for unattended freshness
* Composes naturally with the ambient signal
* Cron catches the "nobody is working but data should stay warm" case

## Performance (validated by adversarial review)

* Morning storm (50 devs at 9 AM): \~50 extra pulls in 10 min = 1% of rate limits
* Steady-state: 4-8% added API load over cron-only baseline
* Scales safely to 500 devs under per-dev API keys

## What NOT to do

* Don't add staleness to agent rules/skills (tool owns it)
* Don't add retry infrastructure (wrong layer for local-first)
* Don't remove the cron (different purpose)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.beads/last_pull` file written on every successful pull
- [ ] `bd linear sync --pull-if-stale` implemented with configurable threshold
- [ ] `--pull-if-stale` is a no-op if data is fresh (5-min debounce)
- [ ] `bd prime` auto-pulls when stale (>20 min since last pull)
- [ ] Staleness warning emitted on stderr for first `bd` invocation per session when stale
- [ ] Warning suppressed after first emission in session
- [ ] JSON output includes `is_fresh` boolean for agent consumption
- [ ] Per-session (5) and per-hour (8) pull caps prevent runaway loops

title: Build CI worker for centralized Linear push (org-internal)
description:
Create .github/workflows/linear-sync.yml (or org's equivalent). Triggers on push events to main that touch .beads/issues.jsonl (NOT .beads/external_refs.json — see [PLAN.md](<http://PLAN.md>) §5 external_ref storage separation). Steps: bd import from JSONL → bd linear sync --push --json → write .beads/external_refs.json → commit external_refs.json back to main → archive sync_history JSON. OAuth client-credentials in CI secrets. Lives in beads-to-linear repo (org-internal, not upstream).

## Acceptance criteria

* Workflow triggers only on .beads/issues.jsonl changes (not external_refs.json)
* Concurrency group serializes runs: `concurrency: { group: linear-sync-${{ github.repository }}, cancel-in-progress: false }`
* No self-triggering loop: CI commits to external_refs.json which does NOT trigger the workflow
* Workflow runs end-to-end on a no-op push event
* Push event with new bead creates issue in Linear
* Push event with bead update updates Linear
* External_refs written to .beads/external_refs.json (format per [PLAN.md](<http://PLAN.md>) §5)
* sync_history JSON archived as CI artifact
* Failed runs surface via existing CI alerting
* Push-volume sanity check: refuse to push if delta exceeds configurable threshold (default 100 issues) — prevents accidental floods
* Bead disappearance handling: when a bead is in external_refs.json but absent from issues.jsonl, archive the corresponding Linear issue (decision d12)
* README documents trigger behavior, CI secrets required, and concurrency behavior

## Non-goals

* Not implementing webhook-style triggers (charter forbids upstream; org choice for org-internal)
* Not implementing parallel workers (sequential is fine until throughput is a problem)
* Not modifying bd export or issues.jsonl format

title: Handle Linear issue hard-deletion (404 on update) in sync
description: When a Linear issue is permanently deleted (not just archived), the next CI push attempt for that bead gets a 404. Current behavior is undefined — likely an unhandled error that halts the sync run. Define the behavior: (a) clear external_ref and re-create, (b) log warning and skip, (c) surface error for human review.
close_reason:
Design decision: when issueUpdate returns 404 (Linear issue hard-deleted), the CI worker should:
1. Log a warning with bead_id and former linear_id
2. Remove the entry from .beads/external_refs.json
3. Continue processing remaining issues (do NOT halt the sync run)
4. On the next run, the bead will be treated as a new create (no external_ref → idempotency marker search → create if not found)

This is self-healing: deleted Linear issues get re-created automatically on the next push cycle. The audit log (PR-8) captures the 404 for forensics. No code change needed beyond standard HTTP error handling in the CI worker (btl-wxa), which already has "failed runs surface via CI alerting" in its ACs.

- Require status checks: YES (CI must pass)
- Restrict force-push: YES for all users (protects JSONL + external_refs.json history)

title: Decide: multi-repo CI worker topology
description: When multiple repos use beads with Linear sync, does each repo run its own CI worker (simple, isolated, N workflows), or does a central worker aggregate across repos (complex, one workflow, cross-repo visibility)? This decision affects Phase 3+ expansion. Not blocking for pilot.
close_reason:
Decision: per-repo CI workers (option A).

Each repo runs its own CI workflow triggered by its own .beads/issues.jsonl changes. No central aggregator.

Rationale: a centralized cross-repo worker adds complexity (multi-repo credentials, cross-repo config, single point of failure for all teams) without reward. The CI worker is syncing a ticketing system, not doing cross-repo analysis. There's no cross-repo visibility need that justifies the coupling. Per-repo isolation means teams opt in independently, failures are contained, and credential management is straightforward (one OAuth secret per repo's CI).

value: bd linear sync --push requires BOTH directions of state_map: pull direction (beads status → Linear UUID, e.g. state_map.open=UUID) AND push direction (Linear state name → beads status, e.g. state_map.todo=open, state_map.done=closed). bd linear link sets both locally. CI fresh DBs need both explicitly configured. The push code in mapping.go:ResolveStateIDForBeadsStatus looks up ExplicitStateMap[toLower(state.Name)] — if only pull-direction entries exist, push fails with 'no configured Linear state for beads status'.

linear.state_map entries participate in BOTH push and pull resolution. For push, the code in mapping.go:ResolveStateIDForBeadsStatus iterates Linear states and checks ExplicitStateMap[state.Name.lower()]. If multiple Linear states map to the same beads status, push fails with 'maps beads status X to multiple Linear states'. Also: ParseBeadsStatus default case returns StatusOpen, so any unrecognized status string (like 'deferred') silently resolves to 'open'. Only keep the core 3 pull-direction mappings (todo=open, in progress=in_progress, done=closed) to avoid conflicts. Extra states (Canceled, Duplicate, Backlog, In Review) should NOT have pull-direction name mappings — they'll fall back to 'open' on pull, which is acceptable. Priority 0 (No Priority) also needs explicit mapping (priority_map.0=0) or it defaults to P3.
